app.name: nazar-tray
panel.status.noData: No numbers yet — start a Claude Code or Codex session and they appear here.
panel.provider.notConfigured: not set up on this machine
panel.provider.fix.claude: Claude Code reports its quota to its status line and nowhere else on disk. Run nazar-statusline install to put nazar-tray in that chain — the status line you had keeps running after it.
panel.provider.fix.codex: Codex writes its quota into its own session logs. Start a Codex session and the numbers appear here.
panel.window.detailedTitle: From the official usage endpoint, read by the opt-in detailed-windows mode.
panel.hint.overflow: Windows keeps new icons in the ^ overflow. Drag the bead onto the taskbar to pin it.
tray.hidden.title: nazar-tray is running without a tray icon
tray.hidden.body: This desktop has no tray host, so the icon has nowhere to go — on GNOME that means the AppIndicator extension. nazar-tray keeps running and keeps writing limits.json.
tray.gnome.title: A panel indicator for GNOME
tray.gnome.body: Wayland does not let a window place itself, so the panel opens in the middle of the screen. nazar-gnome draws these numbers in the GNOME panel instead, where the shell places them: github.com/xfurqan0/nazar-gnome
alert.title: {provider} · {window} {percent} %
settings.title: Settings
settings.readOnly: This run was told what to look like, so it will not write your settings.
settings.providers.help: A provider you switch off is not read at all: its files are never opened and its card is not drawn.
settings.notifications.enable: Warn me when a window fills up
settings.notifications.help: Once per window per reset. A window nobody could read never notifies.
settings.quietHours.help: No notifications between these times. The tray icon still changes colour.
settings.autostart.help: Adds nazar-tray to your account's startup entries. It starts hidden in the tray.
settings.autostart.unavailable: The startup entry could not be read on this machine.
settings.statusline.help: Claude Code's numbers reach nazar-tray through a small wrapper: it records what your status line already receives, then runs the status line you had. Installing nazar-tray does not touch Claude Code's settings. This button does, and it shows you the change first.
settings.statusline.installed: Installed. Claude Code runs the wrapper, and the wrapper chains to whatever was there before.
settings.statusline.notInstalled: Not installed. Until it is, the Claude Code windows stay unknown.
settings.statusline.unreadable: The settings file could not be read. The wrapper's own words are below.
settings.statusline.missing: nazar-statusline is not beside nazar-tray. Reinstall nazar-tray, or run the wrapper from a terminal.
settings.statusline.preview: Nothing has been written yet. This is what would change, and a copy of the settings file is taken before it is.
settings.statusline.failed: Nothing was changed. The wrapper's own words are below.
settings.detailed.help: Off by default. With it on, nazar-tray reads the sign-in file Claude Code already keeps, holds the token in memory for one request to the official usage endpoint, and never writes or logs it. Nothing else in this app opens a credential file or the network.
settings.detailed.suggestion: On a Max plan? Detailed windows shows model-specific weekly limits.
settings.usage.perLine.help: Shows the numbers /usage shows; they count every streamed line, about 1.7× the real spend. Off by default: what nazar-tray counts is one message once, however many lines Claude Code wrote it on.
settings.usage.history: Fill history from Claude Code's stats
settings.usage.history.help: Days before your transcripts, as Claude Code reported them (totals only, no breakdown). Drawn apart from the days this app counted itself.
settings.hint.willShow: It will be shown the next time you open this panel.
settings.invalid.thresholds: The three thresholds have to climb, and each has to be between 1 and 100.
settings.invalid.locale: That language is not one this build can show.
settings.invalid.themeMode: Light or dark has to be system, light or dark.
settings.invalid.quietHours: Quiet hours need two times in HH:MM.
settings.invalid.freshness: A reading has to stop being fresh before it starts being stale.
usage.title: Usage
usage.damaged: Unreadable, left out of these numbers: {months}
usage.empty: Nothing recorded in this range yet.
usage.error.bad_range: That range is not one this build knows.
usage.error.bad_window: Those two instants are not a range.
usage.error.no_state_dir: The settings folder could not be found on this machine.
usage.error.scan_failed: The session logs could not be read.
usage.error.store_unreadable: The usage history could not be read.
usage.error.unknown: The usage history could not be shown.
